title: Staged bootstrap Terraform module for private EKS control plane provisioning
creator: Ava Chen
description: Create a reusable Terraform module that performs a staged, idempotent bootstrap of the Redwood Private EKS control plane into customer VPCs. Module must support operatorless bootstrapping, cross-account KMS-backed state, preflight health validations, and a canary upgrade path so control plane upgrades can be tested with minimal blast radius.
acceptance_criteria: Module exports a single clear interface for: VPC inputs, control plane tier selection, IAM role ARNs, and optional init artifacts (bootstrap users, initial node group manifest).
Module runs idempotently: subsequent applies detect no-op when cluster is healthy and config unchanged.
Preflight step executes and fails fast on blocked conditions: missing route tables, conflicting CIDRs, quota limits, or missing KMS key permissions.

Canary mode provisions a small test control plane (or uses a tag-based canary lane) and runs health probes against endpoints, cert rotation, and API server latency checks before promoting changes to production pool.
Module supports remote state in encrypted S3 with DynamoDB locking and an option to use customer KMS or Redwood-managed key, documented and configurable.
Upgrade hooks: module emits outputs for a lightweight orchestrator (existing provisioner) to sequence rolling upgrades and rollback on health regression.

Automated Terraform plan/check pipeline integration: PRs must run a plan and run preflight checklist; module includes a small sentinel of safe defaults to avoid destructive changes without explicit override.
Documentation and a short runbook for operators describing canary flow, required IAM permissions, and troubleshooting steps.
implementation_notes: Design decision: operatorless initial bootstrap using well-scoped IAM roles and temporary assume-role flows instead of embedding a cluster-operator to reduce external process surface area for private deployments.
Use Terraform 1.6+ features: for_each with dynamic blocks for idempotent resource creation and lifecycle blocks to protect critical resources (e.g., EKS control plane logging, OIDC provider).
Remote state: default to S3 + DynamoDB; expose backend config as module input so customer may provide alternate backend. Encrypt bucket using provided KMS key ARN.
KMS & cross-account: add optional kms_key_arn input and clear guidance in docs for granting redwood-platform-account decrypt/encrypt and describe minimal trust policy for state operations.

Preflight checks implemented via external data source (null_resource/local-exec) calling a lightweight Go binary baked in CI that validates AWS quotas, subnets tagged for EKS, and required IAM permissions. Failure should halt apply with actionable messages.

Canary strategy: support two modes: 1) small ephemeral cluster in same account for upgrade verification; 2) tag-based traffic isolation where we provision new control plane with suffix and route a percentage of requests via smart routing (requires integration with routing policy elsewhere). Default implement mode 1 to keep scope inside module.

Health checks: post-provisioning, run kube-api server readiness, list nodes, check control plane metrics (apiserver request latency), and TLS cert validity. Expose these as outputs and CloudWatch/Prometheus-friendly tags.
Outputs: eks_cluster_name, eks_control_plane_id, kubeconfig_secret_arn, bootstrap_status (ok|failed), preflight_errors (list), canary_report_url (if generated).
testing_and_validation: Unit tests for Terraform using terratest harness in CI to assert idempotency across three successive applies.
Integration pipeline that provisions into the private test account with sample VPC fixtures and runs full preflight and probe suite.
Chaos scenario tests: simulate missing subnet tagging, revoked KMS permissions, and ensure preflight fails with clear remediation steps and does not partially create control plane resources.
Upgrade regression tests: create baseline cluster, apply a code-change upgrade path, run canary validation, then attempt rollback and verify state convergence.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (dev): land module in infra-experiments repo, gate by unit/integration tests (owners: Diego, Priya).

Phase 2 (internal canary): enable module for one internal customer account with 'canary=true' and run full probe suite; keep cluster for 72 hours while monitoring resource metrics and control-plane SLOs.
Phase 3 (gradual): open to internal platform teams and 1 external pilot customer; require checklist sign-off and a runbook handoff.
Phase 4 (GA): publish in module registry, update documentation, and link to Redwood Console provisioning flow for Private deployments.
comments: 2026-02-22 - Ava Chen: Initial spec drafted. We need to confirm if the preflight binary can be written in Go or if we should standardize on a Python script to match other infra tools.
2026-02-25 - Diego Morales: Reviewed and agree on operatorless approach; flagged cross-account KMS complexity. Suggest adding a helper module to create the minimal trust policy for customers.

2026-03-02 - Priya Nair (Infra PM): Please add a short checklist for customer onboarding (KMS policy, IAM roles, backbone connectivity). Also request that the module fail early when VPC CIDR overlap risk is detected.

2026-03-05 - Security (Liam O'Neill): Reviewed KMS cross-account plan; require security_review_required and recommend auditable CloudTrail events for state operations. Also suggested limiting S3 bucket ACLs and blocking public access.

2026-03-08 - Diego Morales: Implemented remote-state flexibility and preflight stub; pushed a terratest harness prototype in PR linked above. Tests failing for case where DynamoDB lock role not present; adding clearer error messaging next.
2026-03-10 - Ava Chen: Decided to implement canary as ephemeral small cluster by default to reduce lateral impact. Updated acceptance criteria and rollout plan accordingly.
